requested_parts.part: Home associated or bordering associated targets
requested_parts.reader_evidence_quote: Deploy may target own Presidency home, associated regions, or any region bordering an associated region; never another home or another Presidency’s Company region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and active local alliances for printed strength, then subtract the target and all other regions in its empire (target counted once; Company defense is zero). After every attempt, roll one die per exhausted officer; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not roll losses. Noncatastrophic failures may retry with remaining resources.

grades.question: On successful Deploy how are loot and trophies calculated and control imposed? What changes if Deploy catastrophically fails?
grades.reason: Every requested material part is resolved correctly by this answer; equivalent wording and clear implications accepted. No material contradiction or requested unresolved branch.

requested_parts.part: Four pounds per tower plus faceup modifier
requested_parts.reader_evidence_quote: On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers plus one for Commander. Distribute repeatedly: Commander family first (£1 for Commander and each own surviving used officer); other families clockwise (£1 per used surviving officer); bank last (£1 per used regiment and each used alliance piece). Repeat cycles until loot is gone. Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags in India if it was capital), open all target orders/remove unrest, put new-conquest control token above associated President box, overlay in region and only office card in Vacant Offices; if Elephant faced outward from target, move it inside. On catastrophe Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and member to supply; exhausted officers still check loss; Commander has no office card to vacate.

requested_parts.part: Existing Debt Army and ship expenses including China excluding Commanders
requested_parts.reader_evidence_quote: Expenses are £1 per Debt, each Army officer/regiment, and each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until track end; continue taking them even at maximum Debt. New emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per Company share; each owner including Chairman gets £1 per share. If total dividend cash strictly exceeds expectations, raise Standing one.

grades.question: When Company regions face a Crisis, which regions are attacked, in what order and at what strength? How is defense mounted and what happens on successful defense?
grades.reason: The answer reverses the known printed unequal-strength test, saying defense succeeds rather than the Crisis. Its later matched-defense clause does not cure that contradiction. The independent excess-alliance source gap remains unresolved and precludes Correct even without the reader error.

requested_parts.reader_evidence_quote: A primary Crisis against a Company region is resolved first; then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, ordered Bombay→Madras→Bengal, with that Presidency’s Commander choosing order within it. Primary normal Crisis strength includes unrest in target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only ordinary attack die; each secondary strength is only its region’s unrest. Associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling that strength, or as many as possible. The printed test says defense succeeds if newly exhausted pieces do not equal strength; a matched defense removes all target unrest and awards Commander a trophy. If it defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. For an indivisible alliance exceeding required strength, the summary says the ruling is unresolved. If Commander vacant, Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if that office is vacant; they choose defense and do not gain/lose trophies.

grades.observed_answer: A primary Crisis against a Company region is resolved first; then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, ordered Bombay→Madras→Bengal, with that Presidency’s Commander choosing order within it. Primary normal Crisis strength includes unrest in target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only ordinary attack die; each secondary strength is only its region’s unrest. Associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling that strength, or as many as possible. The printed test says defense succeeds if newly exhausted pieces do not equal strength; a matched defense removes all target unrest and awards Commander a trophy. If it defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. For an indivisible alliance exceeding required strength, the summary says the ruling is unresolved. If Commander vacant, Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if that office is vacant; they choose defense and do not gain/lose trophies.

grades.question: Explain firm trading strategy, when checks and order filling occur, initiative, capacity, repeat-filled revenue and firm value growth.
grades.reason: The unqualified permission to refill any order already filled this turn includes the firm’s own prior fill. Each firm may fill a particular order only once; repeated filling at half revenue is permitted for orders filled by other traders.

requested_parts.part: One trade attempt and ship prerequisite
requested_parts.reader_evidence_quote: Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and needs at least one ship to select a trade strategy (may choose closed home port); Hobnob has no bid/trade/dividends. Managers secretly select strategy and London bid; reveal bids together but keep strategies facedown until Presidency begins. There roll one die per committed £1 and pay bid to bank; any 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ships minus successful dice (1s/2s); a President’s successful trade initiative is calculated likewise. Fill lowest initiative first; President resolves ties, and Company is not automatically first. If President is vacant or never succeeds, firms fill after Commander/Governors’ chance and Chairman breaks ties. Fill open orders only, up to ships+1, from chosen home port along own filled route. A firm may refill any order already filled this turn; previously filled order pays half revenue rounded down. Advance firm Value one per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.

grades.question: In what order does Military Affairs transfer pieces, assign trainees and appoint Commanders? When is an incumbent replaced and does Nepotism apply?
grades.reason: Every requested material part is resolved correctly by this answer; equivalent wording and clear implications accepted. No material contradiction or requested unresolved branch.

requested_parts.reader_evidence_quote: Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers, each an officer or regiment between Armies, remaining in top half. Then assign every trainee to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacant or another family has more total Army pieces than incumbent’s family, choose among families with most pieces; move selected officer to Commander slot and previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

grades.observed_answer: If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it fails. Company Fraud at start of Revenue rolls one die per your officeholder, reduces Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and pays from bank only amount actually removed from Balance.
